title: Washi Still — Bilingual Object Study
description: A Muji-catalog homage that places one centered object inside deep unbleached-paper margins, named by stacked bilingual captions sealed with a hairline rule — hierarchy earned through size and tracking alone, never weight.
philosophy: This template exists for the speaker who believes restraint is a form of respect — for the viewer's eye and for the object being shown. Rooted in Kenya Hara's principle that emptiness carries meaning, it refuses decorative flourishes, bold weights, and competing chroma; the natural color of the photographed object is permitted to be the only accent the slide needs. It is built for household-goods and lifestyle brands whose products need only to be seen clearly, not sold loudly. A noisy conference keynote would destroy it; a quiet buyer briefing or brand-philosophy walkthrough would let it breathe.
goodFor: Single-product spotlight slides in a lifestyle or household goods catalog deck
Bilingual lookbooks requiring stacked Japanese/English or Korean/English captions
Brand philosophy or 'about the material' slides where text density must stay minimal
Stationery, ceramics, or textile brand introduction decks with flat-lay photography
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly reviews requiring dense data annotation alongside visuals
High-energy promotional campaigns relying on bold typographic callouts and saturated color
Multi-product comparison grids with parallel text columns and spec tables
Dark-themed or neon-accented tech and cyberpunk presentations
author: harness

examples.promptCore: Meditative Muji-catalog quietude — a single object rests in open air, its natural color the sole accent against a warm unbleached ground. The composition breathes outward from center; emptiness is not absence but a deliberate carrier of meaning, the surrounding field earning as much attention as the object itself. Stacked bilingual caption lines feel like an archival product label — calm, unhurried, hierarchy earned through spacing and scale alone, sealed with a hairline rule. Avoid visual agitation: no competing textures, no drop shadows, nothing that announces itself louder than the object.

examples.layoutNotes: Twelve-column grid with roughly 15% outer margin on all four sides, preserving the characteristic deep unbleached-paper breathing room. Hero object centered in cols 3–10, occupying approximately the upper 55% of the slide height as the primary visual mass. Bilingual title stack sits below a centered hairline rule in the lower third, with the secondary-language line set at a noticeably smaller scale and wider tracking than the primary. A minimal deck or brand identifier anchors the bottom-right margin zone at the smallest readable scale — no header band, no footer bar.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a single page from a considered object-study catalog — one thing seen clearly inside abundant, unbleached quiet. Compositional rhythm is spare and vertical: heavy visual silence surrounds the object, and a condensed bilingual caption anchors the lower portion, sealed by the thinnest possible rule. Avoid any layered texture, drop shadow, or secondary graphic element that might compete with the object's own material presence. The mood is unhurried reverence — the kind of stillness that slows a viewer down rather than inviting them to scan.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with outer margins of roughly 12–14%; the hero object photograph occupies columns 3–10 and fills the upper two-thirds of the slide vertically, centered on both axes within that zone. A stacked bilingual caption block — primary label above, translated label below — sits centered beneath the image, the two lines divided by a full-width hairline rule that spans only the caption column width. Hierarchy is achieved exclusively through size contrast and letter-spacing variation; no element on the slide uses a heavier weight than any other. A discreet folio index sits at the bottom-right, flush to the margin edge, the only persistent structural fixture across slides.
